t: You're looking at a bronze statue of William III, standing on the south side of Kensington Palace and facing the Golden Gates. William was King of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1689 until 1702, and he ruled jointly with his wife, Queen Mary II, until her death in 1694. The sculptor was Heinrich Baucke, and the statue went up in 1907. It was cast in Berlin and given by the German Emperor Wilhelm II to his uncle, King Edward VII. Aston Webb, the architect, is also credited with designing it. It has been a Grade II listed building since 1969.
